name: LM324DR
title: LMx24 and LM2902 families: quadruple operational amplifiers
summary: Four general-purpose bipolar op amps per package, built to work from one supply with the input range reaching ground, or from split supplies. The family spans the LM124, LM224, LM324 and LM2902 in their A, K, KV and KAV grades, and the newer B and BA versions of the LM324 and LM2902 with a 36 V supply, lower offset and an on-chip EMI filter. LM324DR is the 0 °C to 70 °C LM324 in a 14-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier, gain -3.6
circuits.description: One amplifier of the quad set up as an inverter: the source drives the inverting input through RI, RF returns the output to that input, and the non-inverting input sits at ground. With RI = 10 kΩ and RF = 36 kΩ a ±0.5 V input becomes a ±1.8 V output of opposite sign, from ±12 V supplies.
notes: A ±0.5 V, 1 kHz sine at VIN gives a ±1.8 V output of opposite phase.

circuits.title: Non-inverting amplifier with supply bypass
circuits.description: One amplifier as a non-inverting stage: the input reaches the non-inverting pin through RIN, RG ties the inverting input to ground and RF closes the loop from the output. A low-ESR ceramic capacitor decouples VCC+ to ground; a second one on VCC- is fitted only for dual-supply use, and with a single supply VCC- is ground.

parts.note: low-ESR ceramic, VCC- bypass, dual supply only

notes: 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors go from each supply pin to ground, close to the device; with a single supply only the V+ capacitor is fitted.

circuits.title: Unity-gain amplifier (test circuit)
circuits.description: A voltage follower: the output is tied straight to the inverting input and the input drives the non-inverting input. The output is loaded by CL and RL to ground. Gain-bandwidth and slew rate are measured in it with RL = 1 MΩ and CL = 20 pF (bandwidth) or 30 pF (slew rate).
notes: Load values come from the test conditions of the GBW, SR and B1 rows.

circuits.title: Noise-test circuit
circuits.description: An inverting stage with its input grounded through RS: RS = 100 Ω from the grounded input to the inverting pin, 900 Ω from the output back to the inverting pin, non-inverting input at ground. Input noise voltage density is measured at the output with VI = 0 V.

operation.text: Four independent op amps in one package, frequency compensated, with an input common-mode range reaching the negative supply and a differential input rating up to the supply voltage. The LM324B and LM2902B (and BA grades) are the newer versions: unity-gain stable, 3 V to 36 V supply, 3 mV maximum offset (2 mV for BA), 240 µA typical quiescent current per amplifier and an on-chip RF and EMI filter. They replace every version of the LM224, LM324 and LM2902 directly. The dual B versions are the LM358B and LM2904B.

LM124 grades cover -55 °C to 125 °C, LM224 grades -25 °C to 85 °C, LM324 grades 0 °C to 70 °C, LM324B grades -40 °C to 85 °C, and LM2902 and LM2902B grades -40 °C to 125 °C. The A grades have a lower maximum offset voltage and the K grades a 2000 V HBM ESD rating against 500 V for the LM124, LM224, LM324 and LM2902; LM2902KV and LM2902KAV take 3 V to 30 V where the LM2902 and LM2902K take 3 V to 26 V. LM324DR is the LM324 in the 14-pin SOIC (D) on a 2500-piece reel, 0 °C to 70 °C, marked LM324.

The amplifiers run from one supply or from split supplies, as long as the total is 3 V to 36 V for the B and BA versions, 3 V to 26 V for the LM2902, or 3 V to 30 V for the others, and VCC stays at least 1.5 V above the input common-mode voltage. Supply current does not change with supply voltage. A B version runs straight from a 5 V logic supply with no ±15 V rails needed. The device is on whenever the supply is connected.
More than 32 V on a single supply, or beyond ±16 V on a dual supply, can damage the device permanently; the absolute maximum ratings are not to be exceeded.

operation.topic: Input common-mode range and output phase
operation.text: The working common-mode range runs from ground to VCC - 1.5 V, narrowing to VCC - 2 V over temperature. An input may rise above VCC, up to the maximum supply voltage, without harm. The output keeps the right polarity as long as one input stays inside the working range; with both inputs outside it the output phase is not defined. Below -0.3 V on either input the input current is to be held to 1 mA, and the output phase is again not defined.
Signals may be applied to the inputs before VCC is present, which suits circuits with several supplies.
One output may be shorted to ground indefinitely at TA = 25 °C or below with VCC up to 15 V. A short from an output to VCC can overheat the device and destroy it.

In the functional block diagram each amplifier has a bipolar input stage built from PNP transistors and is biased by current regulators of about 6 µA, 6 µA, 100 µA and 50 µA. The protection diodes from IN- and IN+ to ground are fitted on the B, BA and K versions only.
Gain-bandwidth product is 1.2 MHz and slew rate 0.5 V/µs, typical.

The inverting stage turns a positive input into a negative output and the reverse; the gain is set by the ratio of RF to RI. The supply has to exceed both the input and output swings: scaling ±0.5 V to ±1.8 V, ±12 V is enough. The gain needed is -3.6. Resistors in the kilohm range keep the circuit currents in the milliamp range; RI = 10 kΩ then sets RF = 36 kΩ.

Put 0.1 µF capacitors close to the supply pins to keep noise from a noisy or high-impedance supply out of the circuit. Use low-ESR ceramic capacitors from each supply pin to ground, placed right beside the device; with a single supply one capacitor from V+ to ground is enough.

Keep analog and digital grounds separate and watch where ground current flows; a ground plane on an inner layer spreads heat and cuts EMI pickup. Route inputs away from supply and output traces, crossing a noisy trace at right angles where they must meet. Place the external parts near the device, with RF and RG right at the inverting pin to hold down stray capacitance, and make input traces short: they pick up noise most easily. Guarding critical traces with a ring driven from a low impedance cuts leakage from nearby traces at other voltages.
Automotive (AEC-Q100) versions are the LM2902-Q1, LM2902B-Q1 and LM2902BA-Q1; LM2902-EP is the enhanced-product version; LM124M the military (QML) version; LM124-SP the space version.
